title: SupremeAI Provider Registry
description: Single source of truth (SSOT) for LLM provider capability, error-classification and failover-cascade contracts. One place to declare what a provider can do, how its failures normalize, and who takes over when it degrades. BN: LLM প্রোভাইডারের সক্ষমতা, ত্রুটি-শ্রেণিবিন্যাস ও ফেইলওভার চেইনের একক সত্য-উৎস।

schema_version.description: Registry contract version (semver-ish MAJOR.MINOR). MAJOR bumps require consumer-adapter review; MINOR bumps are additive-only.

providers.description: All declared providers. The id-space is pattern-open (not a closed enum) so new providers up to and beyond the 12-provider target extend the registry with zero schema changes and zero breaking changes to existing consumer adapters.

failover_cascade.description: Global default failover order: first entry is the primary route, later entries are successive fallbacks. Per-provider overrides live on the provider's failover object.

providerId.description: Stable lowercase provider id, e.g. openai, anthropic, gemini, mistral, deepseek, groq, openrouter.

errorCode.description: Standardized failure classes every upstream error MUST normalize into. Consumers branch on this code only — never on raw upstream payloads.

errorAction.description: The single prescribed consumer action for the mapped error class.

status.description: Lifecycle status. planned = declared but not yet integrated; deprecated = still routable but excluded from new failover cascades.

base_url.description: HTTPS-only API base URL. No paths, no query strings, no credentials.

auth.description: Credential POINTER only. The registry never carries secret VALUES — credentials resolve at runtime from the named environment variable (boundary-guard doctrine: name, never value).

header_name.description: Required when scheme is api-key-header (e.g. X-SupremeAI-Key style inbound or provider-specific outbound headers).

env_var.description: Name of the environment variable holding the credential. Never the credential itself.

reasoning_tokens.description: Extended-thinking/reasoning token accounting surfaced in usage.

mappings.description: Upstream-condition → standard-class normalization table. First matching entry wins; consumers MUST NOT interpret unmapped upstream shapes.

upstream_status.description: HTTP status this mapping applies to.

upstream_pattern.description: Optional substring/shape discriminator for statuses that encode multiple failure classes (e.g. 429 with quota vs rate body).

priority.description: 1 = highest routing preference. Cascade builders sort on this, then on id for determinism.

fallback_ids.description: This provider's ordered takeover list. Must not contain the provider's own id; cycle-free across the registry by convention.

retry_on.description: Standard classes eligible for in-place retry. Everything else either fails over or aborts.
